affectedSurfaces: KOTA-hosted workflow and repair-agent authority guards
agent-facing filesystem discovery and read tools
hypothesis: Resolving the configured operator-token location once, retaining both lexical and real-path identities, and threading that path set through filesystem tools and native/KOTA-hosted harness boundaries prevents arbitrary-filename credential material and aliases from bypassing authority protection without weakening existing tool policy.

metricsCompared.name: configured credential path coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: Protection recognized the fixed scope-authority-token.json basename and missed environment-selected arbitrary filenames.
metricsCompared.candidate: Focused direct-read, discovery, recursive-grep, and symlink-alias assertions exercise configured arbitrary filenames through lexical and resolved identities.

metricsCompared.name: harness authority-path consistency
metricsCompared.baseline: Workflow guards and the Claude native sandbox derived credential protection independently and did not receive the active authority configuration path consistently.
metricsCompared.candidate: KOTA-hosted workflow and repair-agent guards, the Claude native sandbox, and the machine-authority sandbox consume the shared configured operator-token path set.

rationale: This is a fail-closed repair for a confirmed high-severity credential disclosure. The run records 426 passing focused tests covering filesystem, daemon, workflow guard, native harness, and execution-sandbox boundaries, plus type checking and focused formatting checks; the repaired symlink tests keep setup errors separate so assertion failures cannot be swallowed.
